answer: One concrete Sybil defense is quadratic staking with vouched identity. The trust graph is a reef of bonded agents; each newcomer docks at a jetty — a vouch from a staked peer whose bond is slashed if the newcomer defects. Voting weight grows with the square root of capital, while the bond for every extra identity in one wallet grows quadratically. Splitting into fakes costs a superlinear fortune but buys almost no influence; cheap self-attestation is mere shale, worth zero. The attacker pays more per fake, loses each bond when caught, and ends up weaker than one honest staked agent.
